outcome: Miyaoka (arXiv:2504.02621, April 2025) proved Chern's conjecture for closed proper Dupin hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature in the sub-cases g=3; g=4 with constant scalar curvature; g=4 with constant Lie curvature; and g=6 with constant Lie curvature — genuine restrictions (special classes of hypersurfaces) of the stated conjecture, not the full conjecture. Several further papers (2025-2026) proved additional restricted cases and moved bounds, but the general conjecture (for arbitrary closed minimal hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature in S^(n+1)) remains open.

ai.basis_quote: During the preparatory phase, we used ChatGPT 5.6 Sol to interpret relevant literature and mathematical tools, including the Blaschke selection theorem and the real analytic curve selection lemma. All mathematical arguments and proofs were independently developed and verified by the authors, who prepared the final manuscript and take full responsibility for its content.

summary: The decisive event is Reiko Miyaoka's April 2025 preprint 'Chern's Conjecture in the Dupin case' (arXiv:2504.02621), which proves the conjecture — that a closed hypersurface with constant mean curvature and constant scalar (or Lie) curvature is isoparametric — for closed proper Dupin hypersurfaces restricted to g=3 (all cases), g=4 (with constant scalar or constant Lie curvature), and g=6 (with constant Lie curvature). Since g for a closed proper Dupin hypersurface can only be 1, 2, 3, 4, or 6, and g=1,2 are classical/trivial, this covers essentially all non-trivial Dupin sub-cases under the stated extra hypotheses, but restricting to Dupin hypersurfaces (a subclass with constant Lie curvatures / conformal structure) is a genuine restriction of the general conjecture, which concerns arbitrary closed minimal (or CMC) hypersurfaces with constant scalar curvature. This is a 'case settled' under §3.1, hence status=partial, resolution_direction=confirmed (the isoparametric conclusion holds, as conjectured), and no counterexample. Beyond this, I found a cluster of further restricted-case and bound-moving papers in the window, none of which resolve the general conjecture: Ge, Liu, Luo, Yan (arXiv:2606.29246, June 2026) prove the case for 4-dimensional minimal hypersurfaces in S^5 under the extra hypothesis that the Gauss-Kronecker curvature is also constant; Ya Tao (arXiv:2605.19495, May-July 2026) proves a rigidity/isoparametric result in S^6 under constancy hypotheses on certain principal-curvature functions, removing a nonnegativity assumption from prior work by Tang-Yan; Tan, Tang, Xie, Yan (arXiv:2609.03711, September 2026) prove a discreteness result for the scalar-curvature values attained under an additional constant-cubic-trace hypothesis (a genuine extra restriction, so this is more marginal — arguably closer to a 'related' variant than a case, since it adds a hypothesis the original conjecture does not carry); and Ge, Tan, Yan, Zhang (arXiv:2512.08342, December 2025) prove a partial (approximate) verification of the second-gap version of the conjecture, establishing a curvature lower bound weaker than the full conjectured bound — this is a `progress`-flavored bound-improvement folded into the same broader picture, not itself a resolution. On the AI question: none of Miyaoka's, Ge-Liu-Luo-Yan's, or Tao's papers mention any AI or computational tool. The September 2026 Tan-Tang-Xie-Yan paper (arXiv:2609.03711) does explicitly disclose AI use: 'we used ChatGPT 5.6 Sol to interpret relevant literature and mathematical tools ... All mathematical arguments and proofs were independently developed and verified by the authors.' Per §6.2, this is squarely `none` — the model was used only to help interpret background literature/tools, not to produce any mathematics that appears in the result — so ai_role is `none` for the record as a whole, even though this is worth flagging as an AI-disclosure incident in an otherwise AI-free cluster of results. I confirmed 'ChatGPT 5.6 Sol' is a real, contemporaneous OpenAI model name (GPT-5.6 family, released July 2026), so this is not a fabricated or misattributed name. The Wikipedia article itself (checked July 2026 per its own edit history hint returned by search) still states the conjecture is 'unsolved as of 2018' and does not reflect any of this 2025-2026 progress — its lead is stale relative to the literature, which is common and does not affect this record's classification.
competing_reading: One could argue the Dupin restriction is severe enough (Dupin hypersurfaces with constant Lie curvature form a special, highly structured subclass with a rich classification theory of their own) that Miyaoka's result is better read as a 'related problem' (Chern's conjecture *for Dupin hypersurfaces*, a named sub-theory) rather than a case of the general conjecture, which would make the correct status 'open' with no_change_found describing only variant/related progress. I read it as a case rather than a variant because Dupin proper hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature are a subset of the hypersurfaces the general conjecture quantifies over (Chern's conjecture is literally about minimal/CMC hypersurfaces with constant scalar or constant curvature invariants; Dupin hypersurfaces with these extra constant-curvature properties are legitimate instances of that same object, just with an extra structural hypothesis satisfied), so proving the isoparametric conclusion for them removes territory from the open cases rather than posing a different question. Similarly, the cubic-trace paper (2609.03711) could be read either as a case (a further restriction within the same universe of objects) or, more plausibly, as a related/variant strengthening since it fixes an additional invariant (f₃) not mentioned in the original conjecture's hypotheses — I lean towards treating it as auxiliary progress rather than the decisive case-settling event, and used Miyaoka's paper as the decisive `event` instead.
what_would_settle_it: A statement from an expert survey (e.g. a future Notices of the AMS or Bulletin AMS article, or an update to the sciengine.com review 'The Chern conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in a sphere and its related problems') classifying whether Dupin-hypersurface results are considered by specialists to be genuine cases of the general Chern conjecture or a separate sub-theory would resolve the classification question. A dated re-check of the Wikipedia article's edit history would also confirm whether/when specialists update the encyclopedic framing.
